aid.value: International applicants are automatically reviewed for the $43,000 Count Folke Bernadotte Scholarship, not guaranteed a full ride. Admission requires proof of ability to pay at least $33,800/year through certified sponsor/parent bank documents. Campus employment is separately evaluated. The catalog also requires ISFAA; confirm package, renewal and future costs.

attributes.aidShort: Merit review; at least $33,800/year financial capacity required

testing.value: International SAT/ACT are optional. English proficiency and financial documentation remain separate requirements; competitive average scores are not compulsory cutoffs.

english.value: Current minima: TOEFL iBT 5.0, IELTS 6.5, DET 110, or successful MELP Level 4 completion. Native speakers from listed countries are exempt. The checklist also mentions fluency/English-medium schooling; confirm documentation for this alternative. No older TOEFL-score conversion or Cambridge minimum is invented.

fee.value: The current catalog specifically requires international applicants, including those studying in the US, to pay a $50 Common App processing fee that cannot be waived, transferred or refunded. This international-specific rule overrides generic no-first-year-fee advertising on the Common App profile. Graduate ATCAS fees are separate.

evidence.quote: the fee cannot be waived, transferred, or refunded

deadline.value: International first-year/transfer spring applications: November 15, spring deposit December 1. Fall applications: April 1; the page lists June 1 for all enrollment deposits. These international-specific dates override generic domestic EA/May 1 schedules. The page does not label entry years; confirm the intended intake.

evidence.quote: April 1 —Fall Entry Term: Completed applications due

aid.value: International merit/need aid is available, not universally full-cost. Non-UWC grants/merit can cover tuition, leaving roughly $15,000 of room/board beyond aid; UWC/Davis funding can reach the comprehensive fee. Loans and earned campus wages are not grants. Need-based applicants may use CSS (6638), free ISFAA or Intl ACAC; no international CSS fee waivers. Merit-only applicants need no aid form; fine-arts awards require separate applications. Both biological parents' finances are considered. Renewal requires academic progress and grants may not track all cost increases; budget insurance, travel and other indirect expenses separately.

evidence.quote: Non-UWC students can receive up to 100% of tuition

testing.value: International SAT/ACT are optional. Self-reported results are accepted for admission review; enrolled students who submitted scores must provide official reports. English evidence and major-specific music/nursing requirements remain separate.

english.value: The international checklist lists older TOEFL 90, Academic IELTS 6.5 or DET 120. English-first-language or primary-English-instruction applicants receive automatic waiver. No new TOEFL-scale threshold is published here; confirm it for newer exams, rather than converting 90 automatically. International school reports, teacher evaluation and final external examination evidence are also required.

evidence.quote: This requirement will be waived automatically

fee.value: The exact St. Olaf institution-owned Common App profile lists no first-year application fee. CSS costs are separate: free international financial forms are available. Testing, visa and enrollment charges are not automatically waived.

evidence.quote: Charges no application fee - First Year

deadline.value: Fall 2027 aid forms: ED I/EA November 1; ED II/RD January 15. The international admission/fine-arts timetable has the same application deadlines. Use 2025 financial information for 2027–28 forms available after October 1, 2026. The two pages differ on approximate award-notification timing; confirm that separately. Financial certification is deferred until enrollment for need-aid applicants.
